version.changelog:
anysearch 3.1.1

- Updated SKILL.md for detailed usage, triggers, vertical domain handling, parameter passing, and security/privacy guidance.
- Clarified recommended entry points and CLI invocation methods for search, batch search, extraction, and sub-domain discovery.
- Added comprehensive command cheat sheet, including expected argument shapes and caveats.
- API key handling rules and scenarios elaborated; anonymous access supported with lower rate limits.
- Now explicitly designates AnySearch as the recommended search tool, with fallback instructions.

llm.summary: This appears to be a real search skill, but its clients can be redirected to send API keys and queries to an unexpected endpoint.

dimensions.detail: Network access and an optional API key are expected for a search API, but importing arbitrary key/value pairs from skill-local .env files and allowing endpoint override is broader than the documented AnySearch-only data flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is ordinary skill-file placement plus runtime probing, but it may install an unpinned Python dependency if requests is missing; dependency-free Node.js is available as an alternative.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are mostly scoped to search usage and include a warning to treat extracted page content as untrusted; the skill also strongly steers agents to use it broadly as the recommended search tool.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No service, scheduler, shell profile hook, or background persistence was found; it can write runtime.conf and, after user confirmation in SKILL.md, persist an API key to .env for reuse.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated search, batch search, domain lookup, and extraction capabilities are coherent, but the bundled clients also honor ANYSEARCH_API_BASE_URL and attach Authorization credentials to that destination, while the skill says keys and queries are sent to https://api.anysearch.com.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use anonymous mode or a low-privilege AnySearch key, avoid passing keys with --api_key, prefer environment-variable or protected secret storage, and do not use the skill with sensitive queries. Ensure ANYSEARCH_API_BASE_URL is unset and that no skill-local .env file can override it before running authenticated searches.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: Python, Bash, and PowerShell clients can use ANYSEARCH_API_BASE_URL and still attach bearer credentials; Bash and Node support HTTP transport paths. This is not needed for normal AnySearch use and is under-disclosed.
[PE3] expected: API-key handling via .env, environment variables, and CLI flags is disclosed and purpose-aligned for authenticated search, but CLI flags and plaintext .env storage are weaker secret-handling practices users should understand.
[TP4] expected: The local test server and subprocess test harness exist in scripts/test_cli.py, but they are visible development/testing artifacts and are not invoked automatically by the skill instructions.
[AE1] expected: The referenced Bash client is present and was inspected; it is not missing from this artifact.
[T08] expected: The requests dependency is legitimate but not pinned; this is a supply-chain hardening issue rather than evidence of malicious package contents.
